blogs.title: TTAB Must Apply Consistent Definitions of 'Similar Goods' Across DuPont Factors
blogs.description: This post analyzes the Federal Circuit's holding that the TTAB committed legal error by applying a narrower definition of 'similar goods' when evaluating third-party marks under DuPont Factor 6 than it did when evaluating the parties' services under Factor 2. The court emphasized that the scope of similarity must remain consistent across all factors to ensure a coherent likelihood-of-confusion analysis.

blogs.title: Interdependence of DuPont Factors: Why a Remand on Mark Strength Necessitated Reconsideration of Commercial Impression
blogs.description: This post examines the court's reasoning for vacating Factor 1 (similarity of marks) alongside Factor 6 (number and nature of similar marks). The analysis highlights the holistic nature of the DuPont test, specifically how a determination of mark strength based on third-party evidence directly influences the commercial impression of the marks in question.

blogs.title: The Scope of Financial Services in Trademark Law: Credit Cards vs. Banking
blogs.description: This post discusses the affirmed finding that credit card services and general banking services are highly similar for trademark purposes. It explores the implications of this holding for fintech companies and traditional banks, particularly regarding how the Trademark ID Manual and dictionary definitions inform the 'similarity of goods' inquiry in the financial sector.
